newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Empire, Megaworld up for 2nd day.
newsitem.headline: Empire, Megaworld up for 2nd day.

text.p: Empire East Land Holdings Inc and parent company Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc climbed to intra-day highs in late Thursday trade as investors increasingly ignored rumours of financial problems at the firms, brokers said.
Empire rose by 28.42 percent to 6.10 pesos while Megaworld jumped 25 percent to six pesos.
"Investors may have disregarded those rumours and opted to buy, also because of the low prices," said Spencer Yap, analyst at BPI Securities Corp.
Earlier this week, Empire hit a record low of 3.20 pesos while Megaworld tumbled to its lowest this year at 3.50 when rumours were swirling through the market about possible bankruptcy.
Both the companies and government officials denied either firm was in financial difficulty.
"These two companies have said there is nothing wrong with them so buying was seen yesterday and once again today," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
"I believe it's about time we laid all these rumours to rest so we can focus on delivering profits for our shareholders," Megaworld president Andrew Tan said in a television interview.
He also said the Philippines was unlikely to follow the slump in the Thailand property sector.
